decisions: The filed hypothesis ('segment-only analysis may recover call edges while omitting RIP-relative data references') is UPHELD as a symptom description and as a mechanism.

The refuter's line reading is off by one branch and the conclusion is unaffected, which is worth recording so the next reader is not confused. It says exec is empty on a section-less image and therefore sections_are_runtime is false. It is not: entry::executable_sections already falls back to PF_X PT_LOAD segments, so exec is non-empty, the seeds land in it and sections_are_runtime is TRUE. mapped is empty for the other reason -- mapped_ranges itself iterates file.sections(). That matters for the fix: gating on sections_are_runtime would have been the wrong lever, and the one-line change belongs inside mapped_ranges.

The ET_REL guard is left exactly as it is, per the refutation. A relocatable object HAS sections that describe a different address space, so it never reaches mapped_ranges at all -- sections_are_runtime is false for it because no seed lands in a pre-link section. The fallback is therefore reachable only when there is no section table, which is the one case where the PT_LOAD table IS the runtime layout.

A PT_LOAD with p_vaddr 0 is included rather than skipped, unlike the section arm's `lo == 0` guard. The two zeros mean different things: a section at address 0 is unallocated pre-link metadata, while a PIE's first PT_LOAD genuinely maps at 0. Including it is also inert, since looks_like_address rejects everything under 4096.

No option, no phases.toml row, no catalog counter and no tests/stages case: tooling track, and this is a strict wrong-output fix in the read-only reference index that cannot change emitted C -- confirmed by the byte-identical decompile-all sweep, not assumed.

The free riders the refutation predicted are structurally un-blinded too: kuna_poolref and kuna_picbase read the same `mapped` and are inert while it is empty, so a section-less ARM image's literal-pool references and a section-less i386 PIC image's GOT-relative ones now have a range list to be classified against. Neither swept image exercises them -- KataVM_L1 is x86-64 and the trace-p crackme is a non-PIE i386 ET_EXEC -- so the un-blinding is claimed as reachability, not as a measured gain.

The acceptance was retargeted from the dataset witness to a vendored twin before promotion, following corrupt-elf-section-table. It was run and passed against the dataset original first, so the retarget trades reach for portability and not for a weaker claim.
